catalogue.orientation: Landscape-oriented composition within a portrait page

formalObservation.Composition:
A multi-figure scene occupying the central portion of the page.

Principal elements:

- large figure toward the left
- large figure toward the right
- smaller figure or form between them
- broad irregular form extending across the upper portion
- heavily worked horizontal ground area along the bottom

The two principal figures are substantially different in construction.
formalObservation.Primary Forms:
- Large left-hand figure
- Large right-hand figure
- Smaller central/lower form
- Upper horizontal irregular form
- Lower ground structure
formalObservation.Visible Anatomical Features:
Left figure:

- Eye
- Nose/facial projection
- Mouth
- Head/face contour
- Large rounded lower body form

Right figure:

- Single visible eye
- Horizontal mouth
- Multiple triangular tooth-like marks
- Head
- Lower body

Smaller central form:

- Small head-like circular form
- Eye-like marking
- Short projecting element
formalObservation.Structural Forms:
- Rectangular/arched enclosing structures
- Horizontal elements
- Vertical supports
- Rounded forms
- Irregular overhead form
- Dense ground band
formalObservation.Repeated Forms:
- Circular forms
- Vertical strokes
- Horizontal bands
- Triangular marks
- Parallel hatching
formalObservation.Mark-Making:
- parallel directional hatching
- thick charcoal contours
- dense filled passages
- repeated diagonal marks
- loose irregular strokes
- lighter linear construction
formalObservation.Figure–Ground Relationship: Strong separation between principal figures and paper ground, although surrounding hatching visually connects figures to the broader field.
formalObservation.Formal Language:
- Organic and geometric forms coexist.
- Figures are constructed from simplified component shapes.
- The two dominant figures use noticeably different structural vocabularies.
- Repeated circular forms appear within the composition.
- Dense hatching establishes visual continuity across otherwise separate elements.
- A horizontal ground zone anchors the composition.
